newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 26.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Apart from high school teachers, a barrage of other demands from a dozen public service sectors is buffeting the government: any concession to the teachers, now prepared for a seventh week of their strike, would open the flood-gates for other demands, sources say.
--Kostas Karamanlis, a conservative opposition New Democracy deputy, will announce his intention to stand for the leadership of the party tomorrow, according to reports.

--Athens and Nicosia condemned the attempt by a number of EU partners to give the Turkish Cypriot regime an equal say in talks for Cyprus's entry to the EU. Changes to decisions made by the EU, Athens' government spokesman said, will make the EU's eastwards expansion "extremely difficult".

--ND leader Miltiades Evert appears to be losing ground in his bid to win the presidency of the main opposition party. Yesterday, he lost the support of "Eleftheros Typos", the pro-opposition newspaper and a deputy who was one of his most loyal lieutenants.

--A consortium of four construction companies "Athens Casino" has withdrawn its suit against the government over the withdrawal of the licence for a casino to be built at the seaside district of Floisvos. Development ministry sources say the move came after the realisation that the case would lose.

--In a briefing for foreign journalists, Turkish military figures have claimed dozens of Greek islands, some as far from Turkey as Crete, as of questioned ownership, continuing, Athens says, Ankara's standing policy of increasing tension in the Aegean and dragging Greece into talks over sovereign rights.
--The recent surge on the Athens bourse has also given a boost to "high risk" and "doubtful value" shares, the Wall Street Journal reports. At the bourse, there is talk of a "black list" of shares.
--Following barbaric dog-fights in northern Greece, hundreds of Athenians demonstrated downtown yesterday to call for protection of animals.
--The continuing strike by high school teachers has put a question mark over whether there will be annual exams for students in senior high school. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
